newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes, esp sour, gain on Cano shutdown.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes, esp sour, gain on Cano shutdown.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices gained on Tuesday, especially sour grades, after Occidental Petroleum declared force majeure on its Cano Limon field in Colombia following rebel attacks on its main pipeline, traders said.

U.S. Benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing gained more than 60 cents during the regular futures session, quoted at around $19.60/65 late the day, mainly in reaction to the Colombian news traders said.
The West Texas Sour/Midland discount to WTI/Cushing shrunk to as low as $1.09 traded, down from levels around $1.35 under late last week.
"The move is overdone, no doubt about it. But it's the first time this (Colombian rebel) situation has led to force majeure," said a trader for a major oil company.
Colombian state oil company Ecopetrol has had force majeure on loadings in place since July 6 after a string of rebel attacks on the 250,000 barrel per day (bpd) Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline.

Oxy's move on Tuesday, however, was the first time ever that the company declared force majeure on the 180,000 bpd field. The action frees the firm from its obligations to employees and contractors on the site.
At least two U.S. refiners, Amoco and Exxon, have been looking for alternative crude to make up for delays on their Cano loadings.
Sour grades felt the effect most.
"It's Cano that's affecting sours, the rest of the stuff is just hitching a ride," a Gulf Coast trader said.
Eugene Island changed hands at minus $1.30 a barrel, up a nickel on the day.
Among sweet grades, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James last moved at plus 27 cents, up seven cents from earlier today.
WTI/Midland was done as high as minus 20 cents, compared with minus 27 cents on from Monday.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/St. James was placed at minus 30 cents, up slightly.
WTI/Cushing Posting Plus was last traded at $1.90 a barrel, up from $1.85 this morning.
--Tony McAuley, Patricia Garip-Bertuol NY Energy Desk ((+1 212 859 1620))
